text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Some 72,000 privatisation bonds have changed hands since the beginning of the year, but volume of anonymous trades totalled only 4,419 bonds. The market has registered 347,714 orders to sell the bonds.

- Slovakia's sole tyre producer Matador Puchov expects a 1997 consolidated turnover of 13.4 billion crowns, with sales totalling around 9.6 billion crowns. The company plans investment programmes worth around 590 million crowns in 1997.
- Matador's main customer this year will be the Czech car producer Skoda, which will purchase 600,000 tyres for its Felicia model and an unspecified amount for the Octavia.

- Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic said he would prefer parliament's extraordinary session, interrupted last December and expected to resume this March, to discuss both the change to the presidential electoral system and the law barring bank privatisation.
- Ivan Saktor, President of the Confederation of Trade Unions, said it would be premature to talk about a general strike though he did not rule out the possibility.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Real wages and pensions have fallen by around 60 percent since the fall of communism in 1989.
- Illegal software accounts for about 85 percent of all copies of programmes distributed in Slovakia.

SME - Eva Zelenayova, a deputy for the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia, said the government was not likely to link a vote on the law halting the bank sell-off with a non-confidence vote against the cabinet.
- Opposition parties said more than 450,000 citizens had signed the petition for a referendum on direct presidential elections.
PRAVDA - Jan Cuper, a member of the parliament for HZDS, said attempts by the opposition to initiate direct presidential elections were designed to eliminate the powers of the parliament.
